models.inverse_notes: Forward solves CBR from B and P. Inverse B = CBR * P / 1000 needs known CBR and P with P > 0; inverse P = B * 1000 / CBR needs B and CBR with CBR > 0 (CBR = 0 with B = 0 leaves P underdetermined; CBR = 0 with B > 0 is inconsistent). assumptions: Source assumption: all stocks and flows use the same reference area, residency definition and period: P0 is the start-of-period (1 January) usually-resident stock, P1 the next 1-January stock, and B/D/I/E are flows during year T in that area (Eurostat DEMOBAL/Unidemo timing).

Application profile: natural change is B - D and net migration is I - E; Eurostat notes published net migration can include a statistical adjustment residual, so I - E here means measured migration flows, with any adjustment disclosed rather than silently absorbed.
Source assumption: each live birth, death, immigration and emigration event changes the usually-resident stock by one person; the identity counts persons, not cases with multiple counting.

gaps: New meanings initial/final population and period immigration/emigration counts are absent from the supplied runtime vocabulary; extension required.
Eurostat net-migration-plus-statistical-adjustment practice means a future adapter may be needed to separate measured I - E from residual adjustment; this record keeps pure measured flows.

models.inverse_notes: Forward solves end-period stock P1 from P0, B, D, I and E with no division, so no singularities. Any single component can be solved when the other five are known, e.g. net migration M = P1 - P0 - B + D with M = I - E, or B = P1 - P0 + D - I + E. Substitution check: P1 = 1005000 with P0 = 1000000, D = 9000, I = 5000, E = 3000 gives B = 12000, matching reference balance-ordinary. Nonnegativity guards persist per component; a derived negative component flags inconsistent inputs. Algebraic rearrangement does not imply causal direction.
limitations: Does not enforce a nonnegative result: inputs satisfying the guards can still imply a negative P1, which flags inconsistent or out-of-scope inputs rather than a valid stock.
Explains nothing by itself: the identity separates accounting from causal or forecast claims about why births, deaths or migration took the supplied values.

Migration residuals are out of scope: Eurostat net migration plus statistical adjustment can bundle coverage error with I - E, and Hageman notes emigration must often be inferred; this identity uses measured flows only.

references.method: Direct stock-flow arithmetic: 1000000 + 12000 - 9000 + 5000 - 3000 = 1005000; chosen ordinary nonzero-flow case.
references.provenance: Independent elementary arithmetic check with synthetic inputs; no observed population claimed.

references.method: Closed-population check materially different from the open case: 1000000 + 8000 - 6000 = 1002000 with zero migration.
references.provenance: Independent elementary arithmetic check with synthetic inputs; isolates natural change.

references.method: No-change limiting identity: 50000 + 0 - 0 + 0 - 0 = 50000 for any admissible stock.
references.provenance: Definitional boundary check; not an empirical validation.

rejection_cases.reason: Negative births violate B >= 0; a negative vital-event count is scientifically excluded and rejected.
The identity needs all five start/flow components; omitting E (emigration) leaves the end stock undefined.

relationship.locator: Eurostat demo_gind section 3.4 (Population change; Natural change; Net migration) plus Hageman ch.3 per-component growth sentence; corroborated by PRB Balancing Equation entry.
relationship.original_equation: P1 = P0 + B − D + I − E, i.e. Population(time 2) = Population(time 1) + births − deaths + net migration with net migration = inflows − outflows
relationship.translation_notes: P0 maps start-period (1 January) population and P1 the next 1-January stock; B/D/I/E map total births, deaths, immigration and emigration during year T. Signs follow Eurostat: population change is natural change plus net migration, natural change is births minus deaths, net migration is immigrants minus emigrants. No scaling literal and no unit conversion: canonical unit is person (scale 1) for every stock and flow, each event counting one usually-resident person. Dimensional check: population ± population ± population ± population ± population = population. Period handling is by supplied stocks/flows; no calendar-date arithmetic is encoded.
